While these are still incredibly low compared to historical averages, they are significantly higher than the recent past and represent significant capital losses for some investors. Rates have been increasing due to increased confidence surrounding the strength of the global economic recovery, increased fiscal spending in the US, and the expectation that this will lead to higher inflation faster than was previously expected. One of the key tenets of the current valuations of equity markets, especially the mega cap tech companies, has been the comparison to the ultra-low bond rates to support the sky high valuation multiples. As rates have increased, there has been a rotation out of the expensive tech names that were the so-called covid winners, and into the more cyclical and recovery stocks that are expected to improve on the back of an improving global economy. From our perspective, we hope that this is the start of the long overdue rotation out of expensive growth style assets and into the unloved value style assets.
